derived_mir.markers_exact_is_vacuous_here: VACUOUS HERE, and the fixture says so rather than letting the word carry weight it has not earned: `markers_detail` is "0 marker line(s) identical", i.e. there are ZERO marker lines on either side, so `markers_exact: true` is a comparison of two empty sequences. Measured at this HEAD: 1055 of the 1072 A0 candidates are in that same zero-marker position; only 17 have any marker lines at all. This is NOT the same predicate `level::Level::is_zero` fails — that body has real markers that genuinely differ (its `markers_detail` carries an actual diff), so it fails NON-vacuously. A gate reading `markers_exact` as evidence of marker agreement is reading a vacuous truth for almost every candidate. DISCHARGED (partially, and only in the direction that was in doubt) by markers_channel_witness.json, measured from THIS SAME coverage dump: the channel compares 8 real marker lines and agrees on `flat::types::FlatFlags::contains` (which flips), and reports FALSE on `level::Level::is_zero`, whose markers genuinely differ and which the -O gate therefore refuses. So a zero-marker reading here is a fact about THIS body, not an artefact of a dead instrument. It still does NOT mean this body's markers were checked and agree.

bodyful_reachable_closure: PASS — the body makes NO calls (resolved 0, extern_decls 0, unresolved 0), so the reachable callee closure is the body itself and contains no declaration-only entry. This is the A0 criterion that FAILS for level::Level::is_zero, whose closure reaches Option::as_deref / Option::expect. Re-measured 2026-08-13: still 0/0/0, and is_zero still fails — at this HEAD its flip does not fire at all (markers_exact false).

supersedes.what_it_is_not: This was a DOCUMENTED, CORRECTLY-VERSIONED scheme change. It was not silent, it was not a bug, and it is NOT evidence that any compiled code changed: it moved 12,440 of 13,068 per-body digests (95%) while every emitted IR body stayed byte-identical. Every digest pinned before it is a v1 value describing a compiler that no longer exists.
supersedes.why_the_gate_did_not_catch_it: crystal_a1_lineage.rs (and this chain's from_source_system.rs) RECORD the digest; they do not recompute it. They cannot — re-deriving a body lineage digest requires running the trust compiler, which a `cargo test` in this repo does not do. So the two lineage assertions only gate this fixture's INTERNAL consistency: that `lineage` == `flip_event.lineage` and that both appear in `flip_event.raw`. A stale-but-self-consistent triple passes forever. The external anchor is the measurement date plus trustc.binary_sha256, which is why both are pinned here.

link3_build_item.why_this_row_exists: This body was measured NOT CHAINABLE on 2026-08-12 (data/crystal_width_candidates_2026-08-12.json, rank 2). The blocker was LINK 3 and nothing else: Clean's IRConst had seven constructors and no aggregate form, so ir_const_eval had no case for the construct every arm of this body emits. The standing rule is that a lowering gap is a BUILD ITEM, never a reason to retarget the proof, so the form was built.
link3_build_item.also_emitted_by: <tc::expr_location::ExprPathStep as std::clone::Clone>::clone — `const enum.181 { k }`, the SAME shape (arity 1, Int element, depth 1), which is rank 3 of the candidate table and is unblocked by the same build item
link3_build_item.how_it_was_built: An INLINE element spine (aggv / vnil / vcons) inside IRConst itself, following the IRScalar precedent and for the same measured reason: a structural `agg : IRList IRConst -> IRConst` is a NESTED inductive and this elaborator does not register one (eval_ir_state.rs's module doc records the ProbeNested FAIL / ProbeSpine PASS pair). ir_const_value became an explicit IRConst.rec so the spine materializes recursively; ir_const_agg_eval is the typed evaluator and consults ir_ty_is_agg, so an aggregate constant at a scalar type is type_error not_agg; a bare vnil/vcons node is type_error not_agg as well.
link3_build_item.measured_not_assumed: The shapes above were read out of the emitted trust-ir text dump of clean-kernel (dump/clean_kernel.trust-ir.txt) for both bodies, not inferred from the Rust source.
